The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}(1+{a}_{ij}-{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}1+{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}{a}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}{b}_{ij} \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}1)+20-10 \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}1)+10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}1=mn,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}1)+10 & =10\cdot 12+10 \\  & =120+10 \\  & =130.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}(1+{a}_{ij}-{b}_{ij})=130.
$$
